links.outcome: Comparison of zero-shot multimodal LLMs against CNN baselines on the same ECG normal/abnormal task
links.effect: CNN models reached average internal ROC-AUC 0.92-0.94 and external 0.85-0.86, while zero-shot LLMs were near chance (ROC-AUC around 0.5).
links.quote: In contrast, zero-shot LLM discrimination remained near-chance (ROC-AUC around 0.5).

links.outcome: Performance drop from internal test set to external PTB-XL dataset
links.effect: CNN average ROC-AUC fell from 0.92-0.94 internally to 0.85-0.86 externally, a moderate drop; stable discrimination across seeds.
links.quote: Across seeds, CNN-based models demonstrated stable discrimination, with average internal ROC-AUC of 0.92-0.94, and external ROC-AUC of 0.85-0.86.

links.outcome: LLM sensitivity to ECG image rendering (grid vs grid-free) across repeated runs
links.effect: PR-AUC improved slightly with a grid-based calibration background compared with grid-free ECGs; discrimination remained near chance overall.
links.quote: The PR-AUC improved slightly when ECGs used a grid-based calibration background compared with the grid-free ECGs.

unlisted_practices: Physiology-aware CNN architecture aggregating features from anatomical lead groups for ECG interpretation

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the zero-shot diagnostic performance of multimodal LLMs against CNN-based architectures on ECG image classification, evaluating model discrimination without testing specific organizational deployment safeguards or practices.
